evidence.AC1: POST /todos with {"title":"past","dueDate":"2026-10-01"} returned 201 with dueDate "2026-10-01". A POST without dueDate returned 201 with dueDate null. The date is a plain calendar date with no time.
evidence.AC2: PATCH /todos/2 with {"dueDate":"2026-11-11"} returned 200 and the new date. PATCH with {"dueDate":null} returned 200 with dueDate null, so the date was removed.
evidence.AC3: POST with dueDate "2026-02-30", "30.02.2026", "abc" and the number 20260101 returned 400 each time. PATCH /todos/3 with "2026-02-30", "30.02.2026" and "abc" returned 500 with a FormatException stack trace instead of 400. Invalid dates are rejected with 400 only on create, not on update.
evidence.AC4: GET /todos?overdue=true, ?filter=overdue and ?overdue=1 all returned the full list of 5 todos, including a not-overdue todo and a done todo. GET /todos/overdue returned the 404 page. No API way to get only overdue todos exists.
evidence.AC5: The GET / HTML lists '(fällig: 2026-10-01)', '(fällig: 2026-10-02)' and '(fällig: 2026-10-23)' next to the todos that have due dates. Todos without a due date show none.
evidence.AC6: On GET /, today is 2026-10-23. Only the not-done todo due 2026-10-01 carries the 'überfällig' marker. The done todo due 2026-10-02, the todo due today, the future todo and the todo without a date have no marker.
evidence.AC7: The rendered page contains no 'nur überfällige' text; grep count was 0. The page diff adds no filter control. Nothing was found to click, so the filter could not be exercised.
